turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
Now I have enough to answer confidently. Let me quickly check how `internal/ghx` (the Read function) invokes `mapengine.Map` to complete the wiring picture.I have everything needed to give a complete, verified answer.

## Structural map engine

**Location:** `internal/mapengine/` — a standalone Go package with four files:

- **`types.go`** — the engine contract and dispatcher. Defines `Engine` (`auto`/`go-ast`/`regex`/`tree-sitter`), `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`, and the `Mapper` interface. Entry point is `Map(path, content, opts)` (types.go:125), which normalizes options via `NormalizeOptions`/`normalizeEngine` and dispatches by `opts.Engine`.
- **`goast.go`** — `GoASTMapper` (struct, `Map` method), built on Go's stdlib `go/ast`/`go/token`. Extracts top-level declarations (`goASTSymbols`, `goGenDeclSymbols`, `goFuncDeclSymbol`, `goTypeSymbol`), preserving full multi-line signatures and generics, and resolves method receivers (`receiverTypeName`) to populate a `Parent` field.
- **`treesitter.go`** — `TreeSitterMapper`, wrapping the [gotreesitter](https://github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter) library (`grammars.LangEntry`, `gotreesitter.Tagger`/`Tag`). Per-language config (`TreeSitterLanguageConfig`, `defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs`) controls tag→`Kind` mapping, signature extraction, and whether tree-sitter output gets merged with regex-derived symbols. Captures class/impl methods and populates `Parent` (`computeTreeSitterParents`) the way regex can't.
- **`regex.go`** — `RegexMapper`, the universal fallback. Per-language `regexRule` tables (`regexRules`, `typeScriptRules`) matched line-by-line (`matchLine`, `rulesForPath`).

## Engine selection per file

Selection happens in `types.go`, function `Map` → `mapAuto` (types.go:143), by file extension (`filepath.Ext(path)`), when the caller's `Options.Engine` is `auto` (the default):

```go
func mapAuto(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
	case ".go":
		result, err := GoASTMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
		if err == nil { return result, nil }
		fallback, _ := RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)   // fallback on AST failure
		fallback.Fallback = true
		return fallback, nil
	case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
		return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, false)
	default:
		return RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
	}
}
```

- `.go` → `GoASTMapper` (falls back to `RegexMapper` if AST parsing errors).
- `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → `TreeSitterMapper`, via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback` (types.go:160), which itself falls back to `RegexMapper` on any tree-sitter error (including `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`).
- Everything else → `RegexMapper` directly.

If the caller sets `Options.Engine` explicitly (`regex` or `tree-sitter`), `Map` skips `mapAuto` and dispatches straight to that mapper (with tree-sitter still falling back to regex on failure).

**CLI wiring:** `internal/cli/ghx.go` reads a `--map-engine` flag (default `"auto"`, help text `"auto|regex|tree-sitter"`, ghx.go:211) into `mapEngine` (ghx.go:112), passed down as `ReadOpts.MapEngine`. `internal/ghx/read.go:187` calls `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: mapengine.Engine(opts.MapEngine), ...})` when `opts.Map` is true, and reports the actual engine used back to the caller via `result.MapEngine = string(mapResult.Engine)`.

**Not verified:** I did not read `goast.go`, `regex.go`, or `treesitter.go` in full (only their signature maps and the grep excerpts above), so internals like the exact tree-sitter grammar loading mechanism or the complete regex rule tables are unconfirmed beyond what's shown. I also did not check `internal/codemode/` or the MCP server path for any separate engine-selection logic — the README states `--map` and codemode share the same `internal/ghx` read path, but I didn't trace that call site.

README:
# ghx — GitHub Code Exploration for AI Agents

One command does what takes 3-5 API calls. Batch file reads, code maps, search — all via `gh` CLI. Write JS programs that compose operations in one round-trip.

## Why

An agent wants to understand `packages/shadcn/src/utils/` in [shadcn-ui/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui):

**With `gh` CLI** — 4 turns, 4 API calls, reads 3 full files (3,761 tokens), sees 3 of 34 files:
```
gh api /repos/shadcn-ui/ui/contents/packages/shadcn/src/utils       → JSON with shas, urls, links (480 tokens for a file list)
gh api /repos/.../get-config.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (1,981 tokens — agent only needed exports)
gh api /repos/.../registries.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (676 tokens)
gh api /repos/.../frameworks.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (624 tokens)
```

**With ghx** — 2 turns, 2 API calls, maps 10 files (3,058 tokens), sees signatures of all 10:
```
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui packages/shadcn/src/utils                     → directory listing (199 tokens)
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui "packages/shadcn/src/utils/*.ts" --map        → signatures of 10 files (2,859 tokens)
```

Same token budget. The `gh` agent read 3 full files. The ghx agent saw the structure of 10 — imports, exports, function signatures — and knows which ones to drill into. Pass a file, get content. Pass a directory, get a listing. Pass a glob, get matching files. Same command, always useful output.
